elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The affiliate assignment exception is omitted; affiliate assignments remain subject to the other party's prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to a successor organization by merger upon written notice, without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Customer may assign to a successor organization by acquisition upon written notice, without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The exception does not expressly cover a sale of substantially all assets, and a generic reference to an acquisition does not clearly establish that right.

elements.element: Vendor must obtain Customer's consent for every assignment.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign to a successor organization by merger, consolidation, or acquisition merely upon written notice to Customer.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: For Vendor assignments requiring consent, the clause states that the other party's consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: There is no competitor prohibition; Vendor could assign to a competitor with consent or under the successor exception.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right based on Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no termination right triggered by Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The successor exception permits either party, including Customer, to assign to a successor organization without consent.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor exception expressly requires written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The successor exception permits either party, including Vendor, to assign to a successor organization without consent.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor exception expressly requires written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's prior written consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires the other party's prior written consent, subject only to the stated successor exception.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Customer assignment.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent requirement expressly states that consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's prior written consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence applies mutually and requires Customer's prior written consent, subject only to the successor exception.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent requirement expressly states that consent may not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative redline fully reaches the fallback by creating mutual successor-assignment rights on written notice and mutual, reasonableness-qualified consent requirements for other assignments. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits an affiliate exception and an express substantially-all-assets exception, allows Vendor successor assignments without Customer consent, and contains no competitor prohibition. The changes are confined to those needed for the fallback; the pre-existing void-assignment and Customer continuing-liability provisions remain effective and do not contradict the assignment mechanism.
